alignments.note: Aorist imperative rendered by the single verb.
Genitive pronoun realized by the possessive; the vocative phrase is anarthrous, so no article competes and rule 20's displacement question does not arise.
Attributive adjective in the vocative address.
Anarthrous vocative; ASV reorders it after the modifiers (rule 15). No supplied address word, so rule 89 is not in question.

Ordinary negative realized by *not*. Rules 44 and 64 do not reach it: this is `ou`, not an interrogative particle, and the question is marked by English inversion with do-support, which rides with the verb under rule 9.
Article before *God* has no English realization; the ASV supplies no determiner of any kind, so rule 23 and not rules 51 or 60 decides it.
Subject noun.

Inflected verb with the do-support auxiliary English interrogative inversion requires; head on the lexical verb (rules 9, 17). Discontinuous across the negative and subject under rule 15, absorbing neither.

Substantival article governing an adjective, not a participle, so rule 32 does not split off the relativizer: as in rule 31's no-verb carve-out the article keeps *them that*, and the supplied copula goes to the adjectival predicate under rule 53. Competing reading: give *that are poor* whole to the adjective on rule 92's analogy, but that rule is scoped in terms to an expressed predicate noun.
Adjectival predicate takes the supplied copula (rule 53, `homoia` -> *were like*); head on the adjective.

Article takes the English determiner with the case frame *as to* riding along, headed on *the* (rules 21, 67). Directly parallel to rule 67's `to euangelion` -> *as touching the gospel*, where the article carries the frame and heads on the determiner.
Dative noun; determiner and case frame already on its article.

Predicate adjective with its supplied infinitival copula (rules 7, 53); head on the adjective per rule 17. The ASV's italics on *to be* are evidence only, and rule 11 keeps them from making the words `added`.
Preposition realized by *in* (rule 36).
Anarthrous noun.
Expressed conjunction.
Second object complement noun.
Genitive article with its case preposition, headed on *the* (rule 21).
Head noun of the genitive phrase.
Relative pronoun, genitive by attraction; the ASV writes a bare *which* with no supplied nominal, so rule 77 heads it on the relativizer.
Inflected verb with its supplied subject pronoun, headed on the lexical verb (rules 9, 17).

Substantival article before a participle supplies the pronoun and nothing else (rule 32); the dative's case preposition rides with it under rule 21, as `tou` -> *of him who* does in rule 22. Rule 36 does not put *to* on `epengeilato`, no Greek preposition being expressed for it to answer to.
Participle rendered as a finite relative clause; the relativizer is its helper (rules 7, 32), headed on the verb.
Object pronoun.

review_notes: Reviewed against nt-greek-verse-v62; returned unchanged in structure. Every unit, head and status of the accepted alignment stands. The only edit is to the s005 note, whose second clause had attributed the interrogative auxiliary to the negative rather than to the verb it belongs to under rule 9.
Partition re-verified: s001-s024 and t001-t034 each appear in exactly one unit, no invented IDs, one unrepresented unit (s006) and no added units.

s009/s010 remains the one materially contested unit and the note names the alternative. The reasoning that decides it: rule 32 splits the relativizer off the article only where a participle follows, because the participle is what carries it, and `ptochous` is an adjective. Rule 31's carve-out therefore governs and the article keeps *them that*, while rule 53's adjectival-predicate clause (`homoia` -> *were like*) puts the copula on *poor*. Rule 92 would give *that are poor* whole to the adjective but is scoped to an expressed predicate noun, and an article supplying a bare pronoun writes no determiner for rule 92 to leave it.

s011 carries *as to the* under rules 21 and 67's article-carrier clause and heads on the determiner, leaving `kosmoi` bare. Rule 67's own example `to euangelion` -> *as touching the gospel* is the same shape, and its warning against carrying a noun-headed reading across from a preposition carrier is why no head on a frame word is in question here.

s013's *to be* is italicized in the ASV. It is a rule 7 helper on the predicate adjective under rule 53, not `added`: rule 11 makes the markup evidence rather than a verdict, and rule 97 is not the case, no variant unit having excluded a fallback here.

The selected variant SBLGNT.JAS.2.5.v006 -> r00-base covers s011 and s012 and carries no FALLBACK EXCLUDED BY EVIDENCE mark, so rule 97 is not engaged anywhere in this verse and rule 12 forecloses revisiting the reading.

s006 is the verse's only unrepresented unit. The ASV writes no determiner of any kind before *God*, so rule 23 decides it and neither rule 51 (supplied indefinite) nor rule 60 (supplied demonstrative) applies.
